A run with `style.color === 'rgb(255, 0, 0)'` produces `<a:srgbClr val="RGB(255, 0, 0)"/>`, not a valid ST_HexColorRGB, from four call sites (text.ts:134-138 buClr, :277-281 solidFill, :284-288 highlight, :291-295 uFill). The value is reachable: packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:150-155 assigns `style.color = el.style.color` / `style.backgroundColor = el.style.backgroundColor` verbatim in `resolveInlineCSS`, called from `parseHtmlToBlocks` (clipboard.ts:272, :372) which the docs TextEditor paste path imports (text-editor.ts:5); slides text boxes mount that same docs editor (text-box-editor.ts:34, :109) and its Block[] is what `textBodyToXml` serializes. The DOCX half of the codebase handles exactly this input with `toDocxHexColor` (packages/docs/src/export/docx-style-map.ts:53-75), whose own comment at :42-48 names the HTML-paste `rgb(255, 0, 0)` case and PPTX import as sources of non-hex color and states that emitting them verbatim yields a schema-invalid document. No equivalent normalization exists on the PPTX side; `escapeXmlAttr` only escapes XML metacharacters. Real, reachable, and blocking under the correctness rubric (invalid export output breaking a core flow).

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as described. docx-style-map.ts:62 truncates `#RRGGBBAA` to its first six digits and lines 66-72 match `rgba(...)` with the alpha captured only by a discarded non-capturing group `(?:,[^)]*)?`, so a fully transparent color (`rgba(0,0,0,0)` or `#RRGGBB00`) returns an opaque RGB triple such as `"000000"` instead of `undefined`. Both consumers treat any truthy return as "paint a fill": docx-style-map.ts:125-128 writes `<w:shd w:val="clear" w:color="auto" w:fill="...">` for runs, and docx-exporter.ts:319-322 does the same for table cells — producing a solid (black) block in the exported DOCX where the on-screen document shows nothing. The path is reachable and unguarded: clipboard.ts:153-154 (and :416-417, :496-497 for table cells) copy the browser's inline CSS value verbatim into the model, and defaultColorResolver (model/color.ts:14-22) passes strings through untouched; a repo-wide search for alpha/transparency handling in packages/docs/src turns up only theme/canvas literals, no normalization that would strip an alpha-0 value before export. Existing tests only pin the non-zero-alpha flattening (`#11223344`→`112233`, `rgba(0,128,255,0.5)`→`0080FF`); the alpha-0 boundary is untested and mishandled. This is a boundary/lossy-conversion correctness bug with visible wrong output, in-lane and non-trivial.

finding.summary: DOCX `w:color`/`w:shd@w:fill` still emit non-hex color strings verbatim — escaping fixes well-formedness but not schema validity
finding.evidence: Line 77-85 now escape the resolved color, and the comment explicitly acknowledges that `InlineStyle.color` "really can hold a non-palette string (DOCX/PPTX import…)". But `escapeXmlAttr(colorHex.replace('#',''))` still emits whatever string arrived. `packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:150-155` copies pasted HTML CSS straight into `style.color` / `style.backgroundColor`, and browsers normalize those to `rgb(255, 0, 0)` / `rgba(…)`. Exporting such a doc produces `<w:color w:val="rgb(255, 0, 0)"/>`, which is not an `ST_HexColor` (6 hex digits or `auto`) — Word typically flags the part as unreadable content rather than rendering the color. The change touched exactly these two lines and hardened only the injection axis; a `/^[0-9a-fA-F]{6}$/` (or CSS-color→hex normalization) check before emitting would make the attribute valid and would make `escapeXmlAttr` unnecessary here.

verdict.reason: The finding claims DOCX export emits non-hex color strings verbatim into `w:color/@w:val` and `w:shd/@w:fill`, quoting `escapeXmlAttr(colorHex.replace('#',''))`. That code is not in this repository. `packages/docs/src/export/docx-style-map.ts:53-75` defines `toDocxHexColor`, which returns a value only for 6-digit hex (line 56), 3-digit shorthand (58-60), 8-digit RGBA truncated (62), and CSS `rgb()/rgba()` converted with clamping (66-73); anything else returns `undefined` (line 74). Both emission sites gate on it: `docx-style-map.ts:121-128` (run `w:color` and `w:shd`) and `docx-exporter.ts:319-322` (table cell `w:shd w:fill`), each pushing the attribute only when the normalizer returned a value. The exact scenario cited by the reviewer — browser-normalized `rgb(255, 0, 0)` from the HTML-paste path in view/clipboard.ts — is named in the doc comment (lines 39-51) and is converted to `FF0000`, not emitted verbatim. Tests confirm: docx-style-map.test.ts:78-100 asserts hostile color/background values emit no `<w:color>`/`<w:shd>`, and docx-exporter.test.ts:116-154 asserts `rgb(...)` normalizes to `w:fill="FF0000"`/`"0080FF"` with exactly two `<w:shd` elements. A repo-wide grep for `w:color`/`w:shd` surfaced no other model-color emission site.
